I did not know at that point in time that Mr. Mate Boban was in Livno on a visit and that he was in the Gorica Monastery at the time. After some time had passed, the driver -- Mr. Boban's driver came to see me at home and said President Boban wanted to see me at the entrance and that I should go to the Gorica Monastery near Livno. I got ready and went to the monastery that I was told to go to, because President Boban was waiting for me there, as well as the commander of the Livno Brigade, Stanko Vrgoc, and one of the priests was there too. When I arrived, President Boban asked me what was going on in Livno, since he had received various information from brigade commanders, the Vrgoc Brigade commander. I informed President Boban about what was going on, and he told me that I should send him a report setting out what I had told him, and that's what the contents of this report are. While I was speaking to him, I know that he looked at me rather strangely -- or, rather, the brigade commander looked at me a little strangely. And when I started writing this interim report, the president -- allow me to finish, please -- the report to President Boban, I thought it necessary to inform the chief of the MP Administration as well and the head of the Defence Department, Mr. Stojic, and I thought that through their chain of command, the -- or, rather, the brigade commander, through his chain of command, would be informing the Main Staff about this, because this -- and that Mr. Boban would call Valentin Coric or Stojic, the Defence Ministry, to ask them why they don't know about this. So I addressed this to the military police because it was my task to write to President Boban about what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. So that give a bit of a background of why you issued this order. Let's just now look at -- why you issued this report. But let's look at the content of the report. We'll start from the beginning: "Military police units from Livno (with others) were engaged in the municipalities of Prozor and Konjic from 15 April 1993 in combat tasks. Around 1100 hours on 4 May 1993, following the order, they returned to Livno. In keeping with tradition (like in other units), we drove through Livno twice, and at the bus station we fired in the air. After that, we went for drinks to the Park Hotel, and afterwards we returned to the base and put down our long-barrelled weapons and MTS." Now, sir, it talks about "we." Is it correct that you were part of this group of MP officers that came back from the combat operations in Prozor and Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the military police. I was not with them in Prozor and in Konjic. As the battalion commander, I only co-ordinated their work in the field. I know that that incident happened. I came later. I did not participate in the shooting, but I know that that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. Could we draw everybody's attention to the fact that at that time the witness was not in command of the 2nd MP Battalion and that he signed the document as the chief of the Department of General and Traffic Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, that's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But, sir, if you drafted this report, why are you drafting it in such a way that it implies that you were also driving through Livno? It says: "We drove through Livno twice. At the bus station, we fired in the air." Why would you report it as "we" if you were -- you were not one of the soldiers arriving in Livno and firing -- shooting in the air?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I received the reports from my own commanders, and that's how I compiled mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. So you're saying that your subordinate drafted this and you put it in the report to Boban; is that what you're saying? Sir, against who had -- against whom had these military police units being fighting in Jablanica and Konjic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the month of April, I believe that they were performing military policing duties in Prozor and Konjic, which means that they manned the check-points there and carried out other regular policing duties. If there had been conflicts in Konjic, they could not have been deployed there. They could not have even reached Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, it talks about combat tasks. In the first: "Military police units from Livno were engaged in Prozor and Konjic in combat tasks." Sir, isn't it true that these military police units were fighting the Muslims in Jablanica and Konjic in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, it's not correct. "Combat," as the term, was used automatically. It was a slip of the tongue. If they had been sent to fight, they would have reached as far as Prozor. They would not have been able to reach Konjic, because if there had been an ongoing combat, they would have had to pass through Jablanica and they would have been stopped already at Prozor. There's no way they could have reached Konjic. And there is no way -- no chance in hell for them to be able to reach Konjic if there was a combat going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, the report says that, you know, "in keeping with tradition, we drove through Livno twice and fired in the air." What is this tradition, where, like in other units, there is the tradition of firing in the air? Could you explain what this tradition is?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's put it this way: When units returned from the field, they fired with their weapons briefly, and that's all. So whatever unit of whatever brigade came back to Livno after having been in combat, that's how they behaved. That was a custom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Some sort of a homecoming victory parade; is that the way I should interpret it? And, sir, let me ask you: By doing this, don't you think that this -- this type of conduct was provocative to the Muslim population in Livno, since they had been fighting the Muslims in Prozor and Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, that's not the case. As you know, the lines were manned jointly by Croats and Muslims, and the celebratory shooting involved both groups. You just said provocations and glory to the homeland. Were you implying that we were trying to somehow honour the homeland by shooting, our own homeland? But that was not the case, because this was not a homecoming victory parade because the lines were manned jointly by Muslims and by Croats, and they did everything together.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. I don't think you can understand that why witness said what witness said because -- if you don't know how the word "homecoming" has been translated into B/C/S. The word "homecoming" was interpreted as "homeland," and that's why the witness provided the answer that he did. And I wanted to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, let's just move on reading the document, because I do think it goes a bit further than the way you describe it. Reading out the third paragraph: "In the Topolino Bar, owned by a Muslim, where Muslim extremists gather, a group of our lads broke glasses that were on the tables and closed the bar." Skipping one paragraph: "In relation to the throwing of the Muslims out of the cafe, everything started after the clashes in Gornji Vakuf. All this is done by units, groups, and individuals, which happens every day, and it's not true that the military police do it. "The military police warned the staff several times to take action against Mahmut Latific, who reports for Radio Bosnia-Herzegovina and spreads lies and extremism. However, nothing has been done, which stirs up indignation in the military police and other units." Sir, were you there at Topolino Bar when all this happened, what's been described here?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I wasn't there. But I'm telling you what President Boban asked me. He had received such information, and when I said "our lads," I meant the entire town of Livno, including the Livno Brigade, the Bruno Busic Regiment, the military police, and I don't know what other units were deployed there. I answered President Boban, and I wrote along the same lines. He had already received wrong information, and he had already created a wrong picture of the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, sir, the way I read this report is that these Bosnian Croat units came back home, and they wanted to teach the Muslims a lesson, so they went to the bar with the intention to make trouble with the Muslim owner, and which eventually led to throwing the Muslims out of the bar. Isn't that what happened?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, that's not what happened, not correct. There were some Muslim extremists in Livno who went against the BiH Army and tried to defy the Croats. Everybody knew that. And there was a man who did all sorts of things under the influence of alcohol. If he had been sober, he would never have done that. So there's -- there was nothing organised. And I'm repeating. Croats and Bosniaks fought together, they manned lines together, and you can check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, it says here: "All this is done by units, groups, and individuals, which happens every day, and it's not true that the military police do it." Why is it said here that it happens every day? Did this happen every day?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you have 4.000 men in uniforms, you can carry out as many controls as you wish, but there will always be a fool who will create problems. You can't control everybody everywhere at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sir, was anyone disciplined for the incident that's been described here in this report?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, as far as I know, the Livno Brigade did receive a few reports from the military police about its troops having been brought in on account of such incidents, and I know that the brigade did institute disciplinary measures against such troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Troops from the Livno Brigade or military police troops?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO ANDABAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, Livno troops. And I say that with full responsibility. I repeat, the military police performed their duties honourably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bos, we shall continue tomorrow. You will still have 55 minutes left, according to the very accurate math of Mr. Registrar. Thank you very much. We will also have redirect tomorrow, which means that you should have finished with your testimony by tomorrow, Mr. Witness. Tomorrow, we'll be sitting in the afternoon, so we'll meet again tomorrow at 2.15. Thank you, everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
